notable_features.text: Czech is a fusional West Slavic language with a rich morphological case system and comparatively flexible word order despite its basic SVO order, with 40 phonemes and marking of 2 tense/aspect categories. It is closely related to Slovak, with which it shares a high degree of mutual intelligibility, and to a lesser extent to Polish. Its vocabulary shows substantial historical influence from Latin and German.
